scope: NeetCode 150 plus original Blind 75 addition, LC377
note: LeetCode public descriptions were used for 144 problems. Seven premium statements were checked through NeetCode public equivalents; their published bounds can differ. Templates are checked separately by check_examples.py.

problems.title: Contains Duplicate
problems.selected_approach: Return whether len(set(nums)) differs from len(nums), or stop at the first repeated value in a scan.

problems.title: Valid Anagram
problems.selected_approach: Compare Counter(s) with Counter(t). Character order is irrelevant; multiplicity is the entire state.

problems.title: Two Sum
problems.selected_approach: Map each earlier value to its index. Look up target - x before storing x so one index cannot pair with itself.

problems.title: Group Anagrams
problems.selected_approach: Group words by their sorted-character string. A fixed-alphabet count tuple is the linear-per-word alternative when that bound is required.

problems.title: Top K Frequent Elements
problems.selected_approach: Count first, then place values in buckets indexed by frequency. Read buckets downward until k values are collected; this meets the better-than-sorting requirement.

problems.title: Product of Array Except Self
problems.selected_approach: Write the product strictly to the left into the output, then multiply by a running right product. No division; zeros need no special case.

problems.title: Valid Sudoku
problems.selected_approach: Check each filled digit in three seen sets: row r, column c, and box (r // 3, c // 3). Validate existing entries; do not solve the board.

problems.title: Encode and Decode Strings
problems.selected_approach: Write length, marker, payload. Decode the header, then jump by that length. Empty strings and markers inside payloads must round-trip.

problems.title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
problems.selected_approach: Put distinct values in a set. Walk a consecutive run only when its predecessor is absent. Starting at every element would repeat work.

problems.title: Valid Palindrome
problems.selected_approach: Filter to lowercase alphanumeric characters and compare with the reverse. Use skipping end pointers only if constant extra space is required.

problems.title: Two Sum II Input Array Is Sorted
problems.selected_approach: Use sorted end pointers; move left when the sum is too small, right when too large. Return 1-based indexes and use distinct positions.

problems.title: 3Sum
problems.selected_approach: Sort, fix an anchor, and run pair search on the suffix. Skip duplicate anchors and duplicate matched endpoints; repeated values can still occupy distinct positions.

problems.title: Container With Most Water
problems.selected_approach: Measure width times the shorter wall. Move that wall because keeping it cannot improve the area as width shrinks.

problems.title: Trapping Rain Water
problems.selected_approach: Precompute the tallest wall from each side. Sum min(left_max, right_max) minus the local height. This direct linear-space version fits the base task.

problems.title: Best Time to Buy And Sell Stock
problems.selected_approach: Treat each day as a possible sale. Store the minimum price so far and the best nonnegative profit. The purchase must precede the sale.

problems.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
problems.selected_approach: Keep a set of the current characters. Shrink until the incoming character is absent, then add it and measure the valid window.

problems.title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
problems.selected_approach: Count the current uppercase letters. Shrink while window length minus the exact largest count exceeds k. Recomputing over 26 keys keeps the rule simple.

problems.title: Permutation In String
problems.selected_approach: Use a fixed window of len(s1). Add its new letter, remove its old letter, and compare 26-element count arrays. Equal counts mean a permutation.

problems.title: Minimum Window Substring
problems.selected_approach: Track missing required copies. Expand until none are missing, then shrink while valid. Store the best range and slice only once.

problems.title: Sliding Window Maximum
problems.selected_approach: Keep decreasing-value candidate indexes in a deque. Remove expired indexes at the front and dominated candidates at the back. Read the maximum at the front.

problems.title: Valid Parentheses
problems.selected_approach: Push openers. Each closer must match the top opener. Reject a missing or mismatched top, and require an empty stack at the end.

problems.title: Min Stack
problems.selected_approach: Push (value, minimum_so_far) pairs. Pop removes both facts together. Read the two fields of the top for top and getMin; all operations are constant time.

problems.title: Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation
problems.selected_approach: Push numbers; an operator pops right operand then left operand. Apply the operator and push its result. Division truncates toward zero, including negatives.

problems.title: Generate Parentheses
problems.selected_approach: Build a prefix with counts of opens and closes. Open while opens < n; close while closes < opens. Save complete strings of length 2*n.

problems.title: Daily Temperatures
problems.selected_approach: Store waiting day indexes. A strictly warmer incoming day resolves and pops colder days. Write index differences; equal temperatures must keep waiting.

problems.title: Car Fleet
problems.selected_approach: Sort by position descending. A car whose solo arrival time is no greater than the fleet ahead joins it; a larger time starts a new fleet.

problems.title: Largest Rectangle In Histogram
problems.selected_approach: Keep (earliest_start, height) pairs. A shorter bar finalizes taller rectangles. Carry the earliest popped start into the new bar and flush with a trailing zero.

problems.title: Binary Search
problems.selected_approach: Find the first index with value >= target. Check both bounds and equality; otherwise return -1. The required search time is logarithmic.

problems.title: Search a 2D Matrix
problems.selected_approach: Treat the row-ordered matrix as a virtual sorted array. Map a flat midpoint with divmod(mid, column_count); do not construct a flattened copy.

problems.title: Koko Eating Bananas
problems.selected_approach: Binary-search the first speed with sum((pile + speed - 1) // speed) <= h. Increasing speed never increases required hours.

problems.title: Find Minimum In Rotated Sorted Array
problems.selected_approach: Find the first index where nums[i] <= nums[-1]. Distinct rotated values make this predicate false then true, even when the array is unrotated.

problems.title: Search In Rotated Sorted Array
problems.selected_approach: Find the minimum pivot, choose the sorted side whose value range can contain target, then boundary-search that side. Distinctness is part of the proof.

problems.title: Time Based Key Value Store
problems.selected_approach: Keep parallel timestamp and value lists per key. Increasing set timestamps allow append. Get uses bisect_right(times, t) - 1; a negative index means no value.

problems.title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
problems.selected_approach: Binary-search the left-half count taken from the shorter array. Adjust until both cross-cut comparisons hold. Use infinities at empty sides; the task requires logarithmic time.

problems.title: Reverse Linked List
problems.selected_approach: Save next, point current.next backward, then advance previous and current. Return the final previous node, including None for an empty input.

problems.title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
problems.selected_approach: Build after a dummy tail by splicing the smaller current head. Advance that list and the tail. Attach the remaining list once the other ends.

problems.title: Reorder List
problems.selected_approach: Collect node references, then relink front, back, front, back. Terminate the final next link. For constant space, split, reverse the second half, and weave.

problems.title: Remove Nth Node From End of List
problems.selected_approach: Keep slow at a dummy and advance fast n nodes from head. Move both until fast ends; slow is now the target's predecessor. Bypass its next link.

problems.title: Copy List With Random Pointer
problems.selected_approach: First create a map from every original node to a fresh node, including None. Then translate next and random through that map. Values are not identities.

problems.title: Add Two Numbers
problems.selected_approach: Walk both digit lists with a carry. Emit total % 10 and keep total // 10 while either list or carry remains. Build after a dummy.

problems.title: Linked List Cycle
problems.selected_approach: Move slow one link and fast two. Meeting means a cycle; reaching an absent fast link means no cycle. Compare node identity, not values.

problems.title: Find The Duplicate Number
problems.selected_approach: Read index -> nums[index] as a functional graph. Floyd finds a meeting; restarting one pointer at index 0 locates the cycle entrance, the duplicate. No mutation or extra set.

problems.title: LRU Cache
problems.selected_approach: Keep keys in OrderedDict recency order. Move a key to the recent end on get and put; evict the oldest on overflow. If implementing internals, combine a map with a doubly linked list.

problems.title: Merge K Sorted Lists
problems.selected_approach: Put one front node from each sorted list in a heap. Pop, append, and replace it with its successor. Include a list identifier to break equal-value ties safely.

problems.title: Reverse Nodes In K Group
problems.selected_approach: Probe k nodes before changing links. Reverse that complete group with previous initialized to the following node, splice it back, and leave an incomplete suffix unchanged.

problems.title: Invert Binary Tree
problems.selected_approach: Visit every real node and swap its left and right references. An empty child stays empty. A stack avoids depth limits if needed.

problems.title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
problems.selected_approach: Build one level frontier at a time and count levels. Alternatively carry depth in a stack. Avoid recursive depth assumptions for a long chain.

problems.title: Diameter of Binary Tree
problems.selected_approach: Process children before parents. Store node-count heights; the edge-count diameter through a node is left_height + right_height. Keep the largest candidate.

problems.title: Balanced Binary Tree
problems.selected_approach: Use the same bottom-up heights. Every node must have child heights differing by at most one. An explicit reversed parent-first order handles deep chains.

problems.title: Same Tree
problems.selected_approach: Compare node pairs. Two missing nodes match; one missing node or unequal values fails. Both corresponding child pairs must match.

problems.title: Subtree of Another Tree
problems.selected_approach: Try every source node as a subtree root and perform an exact paired shape/value comparison. The direct O(n*m) approach fits these limits; use stacks for deep inputs.

problems.title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Search Tree
problems.selected_approach: Walk left if both target values are smaller and right if both are larger. The first split, including equality with a target, is the answer.

problems.title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
problems.selected_approach: Store a list of one level. Save its values, then replace it with all nonempty children in left-to-right order.

problems.title: Binary Tree Right Side View
problems.selected_approach: Use level traversal and take the last value of each level. This is the rightmost node because the frontier remains in left-to-right order.

problems.title: Count Good Nodes In Binary Tree
problems.selected_approach: Carry the maximum ancestor value with each stack entry. Count the node when its value is at least that maximum, then update the value for its children.

problems.title: Validate Binary Search Tree
problems.selected_approach: Carry strict lower and upper bounds from all ancestors. Narrow the upper bound for a left child and lower bound for a right child. Equality is invalid.

problems.title: Kth Smallest Element In a Bst
problems.selected_approach: Traverse inorder with a stack and stop at the kth pop. For many queries with updates, store subtree sizes to guide rank selection.

problems.title: Construct Binary Tree From Preorder And Inorder Traversal
problems.selected_approach: Map values to inorder indexes. Consume preorder roots through subtree jobs on inorder ranges. Schedule right before left on a stack so preorder is consumed correctly; avoid repeated slicing.

problems.title: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
problems.selected_approach: Combine bottom-up gains. Send one nonnegative child branch upward; test both branches plus the node as a complete path. Initialize the best for all-negative trees.

problems.title: Serialize And Deserialize Binary Tree
problems.selected_approach: BFS-serialize values and explicit null markers. Decode with a queue: each real node consumes its two child tokens. Retain shape, negative values, and the empty tree.

problems.title: Implement Trie Prefix Tree
problems.selected_approach: Store a character-child dictionary per node and a terminal marker. Search requires a terminal; startsWith only requires that the path exists.

problems.title: Design Add And Search Words Data Structure
problems.selected_approach: Follow a literal edge; for a dot, try every character child at that position. The pattern must finish at a terminal marker. Use the same trie as ordinary prefix search.

problems.title: Word Search II
problems.selected_approach: Build one trie for all words and DFS the grid through trie edges. Restore path marks, remove found terminal markers, and delete exhausted child edges to prune future searches.

problems.title: Kth Largest Element In a Stream
problems.selected_approach: Retain a min-heap of the largest k values across initialization and add calls. Push, trim when size exceeds k, then return the root. Duplicates count separately.

problems.title: Last Stone Weight
problems.selected_approach: Heapify negative weights. Pop the two heaviest, push a nonzero difference, and repeat. Return the last weight, or zero if all stones disappear.

problems.title: K Closest Points to Origin
problems.selected_approach: Sort by squared distance x*x + y*y and take the first k points. No square root is needed. This clear sorting solution fits the stated limits.

problems.title: Kth Largest Element In An Array
problems.selected_approach: Keep the largest k values in a min-heap. Its root is the kth largest, including duplicate occurrences. Each push may be followed by one trim.

problems.title: Task Scheduler
problems.selected_approach: Fill cooldown+1 slots per round with distinct tasks of largest remaining count. Reinsert updated counts only after the round; include idle time except after the last task.

problems.title: Design Twitter
problems.selected_approach: Store per-author timestamped tweets and followee sets. Merge one newest candidate per relevant author with a heap. After each pop, advance only that author; stop after ten.

problems.title: Find Median From Data Stream
problems.selected_approach: Keep lower values in a max-heap and upper values in a min-heap. Preserve order and a size difference of at most one. Read the middle root or average of roots.

problems.title: Subsets
problems.selected_approach: Start with the empty subset. For each new value, add a copy of every old subset extended by that value. Each subset either contains the new value or does not.

problems.title: Combination Sum
problems.selected_approach: Sort positive candidates and recurse from a start index. Recurse at the same index to allow reuse. Stop when remaining is zero or the next value is too large.

problems.title: Permutations
problems.selected_approach: Choose each remaining position as the next value. Recurse on the smaller pool and extended path. Save when the pool is empty; input values are distinct.

problems.title: Subsets II
problems.selected_approach: Sort and recurse from a start index, saving every path. Skip equal choices at the same depth and recurse at i+1, so each occurrence is used at most once.

problems.title: Combination Sum II
problems.selected_approach: Sort, skip equal same-depth choices, and recurse at i+1. This changes unlimited Combination Sum to one use per input occurrence without duplicate result combinations.

problems.title: Word Search
problems.selected_approach: State is (row, column, word_index) plus cells used by this path. Match, mark, explore four neighbors, and unmark. Another starting path may reuse those cells.

problems.title: Palindrome Partitioning
problems.selected_approach: Choose each next prefix that is a palindrome and recurse on the suffix. A path of pieces is complete at the string end; copy it into the result.

problems.title: Letter Combinations of a Phone Number
problems.selected_approach: Expand a list of prefixes once per digit, using that digit's letter choices. This is a Cartesian product. If an interface allows empty digits, return an empty result.

problems.title: N Queens
problems.selected_approach: Place one queen per row. Track occupied columns, r-c diagonals, and r+c diagonals. Undo all three marks and the board cell after each recursive branch.

problems.title: Number of Islands
problems.selected_approach: Scan string-valued land cells. Each unseen '1' starts one flood. Sink or mark the whole four-neighbor component before scanning onward; count starts, not individual cells.

problems.title: Clone Graph
problems.selected_approach: Map each original node to its clone before visiting neighbors. Reuse existing clones when cycles return to a node. Recreate neighbor links between copies only.

problems.title: Max Area of Island
problems.selected_approach: Use integer-valued flood fill and count each component's cells. Return the largest size, or zero for all water. Mark before adding neighbors to avoid duplicate work.

problems.title: Pacific Atlantic Water Flow
problems.selected_approach: Reverse-flow from each ocean's border, allowing equal or higher neighbors. A cell reaching both reversed floods can drain to both oceans. Return their intersection.

problems.title: Surrounded Regions
problems.selected_approach: Flood border-connected 'O' cells as safe. Flip only unmarked 'O' cells, then restore safe cells. Border reachability decides capture; size and shape do not.

problems.title: Rotting Oranges
problems.selected_approach: Seed every rotten orange and count fresh ones. BFS one level per minute, marking fresh cells immediately. Return -1 if fresh remains after the queue empties.

problems.title: Walls And Gates
problems.selected_approach: Seed all gates at zero distance. BFS into only unfilled rooms and write parent distance + 1. Walls block movement; unreachable rooms retain INF.

problems.title: Course Schedule
problems.selected_approach: Build prerequisite -> course edges and unmet-prerequisite counts. Repeatedly take ready courses. Finishing all courses means no dependency cycle blocks them.

problems.title: Course Schedule II
problems.selected_approach: Use the same readiness process and save its removal order. Return the order only if it contains every course, otherwise return an empty list.

problems.title: Redundant Connection
problems.selected_approach: Union endpoints in input order. The extra cycle edge is the first edge whose endpoints already share a component. Use n+1 storage for 1-based labels.

problems.title: Number of Connected Components In An Undirected Graph
problems.selected_approach: Build undirected adjacency, then count flood starts over all n nodes. Isolated nodes each form a component. Union-find is useful when edges must be processed incrementally.

problems.title: Graph Valid Tree
problems.selected_approach: Require n-1 undirected edges, then flood from one node and require all n nodes reached. The edge count plus connectivity characterizes a tree here.

problems.title: Word Ladder
problems.selected_approach: BFS over one-letter transformations that remain in the word set. Remove on enqueue. Return the word-count distance, including both endpoints, or zero if unreachable.

problems.title: Reconstruct Itinerary
problems.selected_approach: Consume outgoing tickets in lexical order and append an airport only after its exits are exhausted. Reverse completion order. Duplicate tickets are separate edges; validity is guaranteed.

problems.title: Min Cost to Connect All Points
problems.selected_approach: Dense Prim stores each outside point's cheapest edge to the current tree. Repeatedly select the least cost and update Manhattan distances. An O(n^2) scan avoids all-edge storage.

problems.title: Network Delay Time
problems.selected_approach: Dijkstra computes shortest arrival times along nonnegative directed edges. Return the largest final distance, or -1 if any node is unreachable from the source.

problems.title: Swim In Rising Water
problems.selected_approach: Use a heap path cost equal to the maximum height encountered, not a sum. Start with the origin's height. The destination's cheapest popped cost is the required water level.

problems.title: Alien Dictionary
problems.selected_approach: Adjacent sorted words give an edge only at their first differing letter. Reject a longer word before its prefix. Deduplicate edges, include isolated letters, then topologically sort.

problems.title: Cheapest Flights Within K Stops
problems.selected_approach: Run k+1 relaxation rounds for at most k stops. Read only the old distance layer and write into a copy. One distance per city without a move layer loses needed state.

problems.title: Climbing Stairs
problems.selected_approach: Count ways by the last move: ways[i] = ways[i-1] + ways[i-2], with one way to form an empty path. The answer at n counts sequences of moves.

problems.title: Min Cost Climbing Stairs
problems.selected_approach: Define minimum cost to reach each position, including the top at n. Arrive from either previous step plus its cost. Positions 0 and 1 start with zero cost.

problems.title: House Robber
problems.selected_approach: For each house, compare skipping it with taking its value plus the best result two houses back. Start with zero for empty prefixes.

problems.title: House Robber II
problems.selected_approach: Handle one house directly. Otherwise solve the line once without the first house and once without the last; take the larger result because the endpoints are neighbors.

problems.title: Longest Palindromic Substring
problems.selected_approach: Expand around every single-character and gap center. Record the longest matching range and slice once. Odd and even palindromes both need centers.

problems.title: Palindromic Substrings
problems.selected_approach: Use the same two center types, adding one per successful outward expansion. Equal text at different positions counts as different substrings.

problems.title: Decode Ways
problems.selected_approach: Count prefix decodings. Add from i-1 for a valid nonzero last digit and from i-2 for a last pair from 10 through 26. Leading zero is not a letter.

problems.title: Coin Change
problems.selected_approach: Let dp[amount] be minimum coin count. Try each possible last coin; start dp[0]=0 and other entries unreachable. Unlimited reuse is allowed; greedy is insufficient.

problems.title: Maximum Product Subarray
problems.selected_approach: Keep the largest and smallest products ending here. Update both from the old pair and the new value alone. A negative value swaps useful extremes; zero allows restart.

problems.title: Word Break
problems.selected_approach: Let possible[i] mean the prefix s[:i] can be split. Try a last dictionary word after any reachable prefix. Start possible[0]=True; words may repeat.

problems.title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
problems.selected_approach: Default: endpoint DP tries all earlier smaller values in O(n^2), fitting n<=2500. For the logarithmic follow-up, retain minimum tails by length and replace with bisect_left.

problems.title: Partition Equal Subset Sum
problems.selected_approach: Reject an odd total. Track subset sums up to half the total, using only old sums to add the next item. Each input occurrence is used at most once.

problems.title: Combination Sum IV
problems.selected_approach: Count ordered sequences by their last number: ways[t] = sum(ways[t-x]) for fitting positive x. Start ways[0]=1; total-first iteration distinguishes different orders.

problems.title: Unique Paths
problems.selected_approach: Fill a path-count grid from above and left. Initialize the first row and column to one. Only right and down moves are legal, so dependencies are acyclic.

problems.title: Longest Common Subsequence
problems.selected_approach: For prefix pair (i,j), equal last characters extend the diagonal by one. Otherwise take the larger result from skipping either last character. Empty-prefix lengths are zero.

problems.title: Best Time to Buy And Sell Stock With Cooldown
problems.selected_approach: State includes day and whether a share is held. Compare skipping with buying or selling. A sale transitions to the free state two days ahead, enforcing cooldown.

problems.title: Coin Change II
problems.selected_approach: Count unordered coin combinations. Process coins outside and totals upward inside. This allows reuse of the current coin without recounting different coin orders.

problems.title: Target Sum
problems.selected_approach: Cache (index, running_sum). Add counts from choosing plus and minus for the next value. At the end, return whether the target is reached; zero still creates two choices.

problems.title: Interleaving String
problems.selected_approach: Reject a total-length mismatch. State (i,j) consumes i and j characters; the target position is i+j. Either matching source may supply the next character.

problems.title: Longest Increasing Path In a Matrix
problems.selected_approach: Sort cells from highest value to lowest. A cell's answer is one plus the largest answer of a strictly higher neighbor. Equal heights cannot connect; long paths need no recursion.

problems.title: Distinct Subsequences
problems.selected_approach: Always count ways that skip the source's last character; also count using it when it matches the target's last character. Forming an empty target has one way.

problems.title: Edit Distance
problems.selected_approach: Prefix DP compares insert, delete, and replace, with no cost for equal final characters. Empty-to-prefix cost is its length; return the full-prefix cell.

problems.title: Burst Balloons
problems.selected_approach: Use open intervals between fixed padded walls. Try each interior balloon as the last burst and add its two solved sides plus the wall product. Fill narrow intervals first.

problems.title: Regular Expression Matching
problems.selected_approach: Cache input and pattern positions. A starred unit either consumes nothing or consumes one matching character while staying on that unit. Both inputs must finish together.

problems.title: Maximum Subarray
problems.selected_approach: Track the best nonempty sum ending here: restart at x or extend by x. Keep a separate global best initialized from the first value for all-negative input.

problems.title: Jump Game
problems.selected_approach: Keep the farthest reachable index. An index beyond it proves a gap; otherwise extend reach with i+nums[i]. Reaching an index also makes all earlier positions reachable.

problems.title: Jump Game II
problems.selected_approach: Treat a reachable index range as one BFS layer. Its farthest outgoing jump sets the next layer's end. Count layers until the destination is included; reachability is guaranteed.

problems.title: Gas Station
problems.selected_approach: Reject insufficient total fuel. Scan net fuel and restart after each negative running tank. Every start inside that failed segment is also impossible.

problems.title: Hand of Straights
problems.selected_approach: The smallest unused card must start a consecutive group. Consume one copy of each required value, or fail. Count duplicates and reject a nondivisible total first.

problems.title: Merge Triplets to Form Target Triplet
problems.selected_approach: Discard any triple exceeding the target anywhere. Take coordinate-wise maxima over all remaining triples. Equality with the target means they can be merged to form it.

problems.title: Partition Labels
problems.selected_approach: Store each character's final index. Extend the current partition through all final indexes encountered, and cut at the earliest boundary that closes every character inside.

problems.title: Valid Parenthesis String
problems.selected_approach: Track the feasible range of unmatched openers. A star expands both ends, a closer shifts down, and an opener shifts up. Reject negative maximum; finish with zero feasible.

problems.title: Insert Interval
problems.selected_approach: Use the sorted disjoint order: copy intervals before the new one, merge all overlaps, then append those after it. Touching endpoints overlap in this task.

problems.title: Merge Intervals
problems.selected_approach: Sort by start. Merge into the last output interval when start <= last_end; otherwise start a new output interval. Preserve the larger end for containment cases.

problems.title: Non Overlapping Intervals
problems.selected_approach: Sort by end and keep each interval that starts at or after the last kept end. Earliest finish leaves the most remaining room. Return total minus kept.

problems.title: Meeting Rooms
problems.selected_approach: Sort by start and compare adjacent meetings. Fail when a previous end exceeds the next start. Equality is allowed: a meeting may start when another ends.

problems.title: Meeting Rooms II
problems.selected_approach: Sweep start +1 and end -1 events. Process ends first on ties, then take the maximum active count. Return zero for no meetings if the interface allows it.

problems.title: Minimum Interval to Include Each Query
problems.selected_approach: Sort queries; push intervals that have started into a length-priority heap. Pop expired tops and read the shortest valid length. Restore original query order, including duplicates.

problems.title: Rotate Image
problems.selected_approach: Transpose across the main diagonal, then reverse every row. Both operations are in place and realize (r,c) -> (c,n-1-r) for the required clockwise rotation.

problems.title: Spiral Matrix
problems.selected_approach: Peel top, right, bottom, and left edges while shrinking bounds. Recheck for remaining rows and columns before the reverse edges so single rows and columns are not duplicated.

problems.title: Set Matrix Zeroes
problems.selected_approach: First collect rows and columns with original zeros, then write. For the constant-space follow-up, reuse the first row/column as markers with saved boundary flags.

problems.title: Happy Number
problems.selected_approach: Repeatedly sum squared digits. A seen set detects a loop; stop successfully at 1. The same deterministic-state reasoning applies to other repeated transformations.

problems.title: Plus One
problems.selected_approach: Scan digits right to left. Turn 9 into 0 and carry; increment the first smaller digit and return. If every digit was 9, prepend 1.

problems.title: Pow(x, n)
problems.selected_approach: Compute one half-power and square it; multiply by x when the exponent is odd. For negative powers, invert x and negate the exponent. Depth is logarithmic.

problems.title: Multiply Strings
problems.selected_approach: Multiply digit pairs into place i+j in reversed digit arrays. Normalize carries from low places to high places, remove leading zeros, and join digits. Do not parse the whole operands as integers.

problems.title: Detect Squares
problems.selected_approach: Count coordinate copies. For each possible diagonal of a nonzero axis-aligned square, look up the two forced corners and multiply the three stored multiplicities.

problems.title: Single Number
problems.selected_approach: XOR all values. Every paired occurrence cancels, leaving the single value. The exact twice-except-once multiplicity is essential to this rule.

problems.title: Number of 1 Bits
problems.selected_approach: Use bit_count(), or repeatedly count the low bit and shift. The alternative n &= n-1 removes one set bit per step; apply these loops to nonnegative inputs.

problems.title: Counting Bits
problems.selected_approach: Build counts[i] = counts[i >> 1] + (i & 1). The smaller number's answer is already available. Initialize counts[0]=0 for the required linear pass.

problems.title: Reverse Bits
problems.selected_approach: Read the low bit and append it to the result, then shift the input. Run exactly 32 rounds so leading zeros become trailing zeros correctly.

problems.title: Missing Number
problems.selected_approach: Subtract sum(nums) from n*(n+1)//2. Exactly one distinct value is missing from 0 through n; this gives linear time and constant extra space.

problems.title: Sum of Two Integers
problems.selected_approach: Iterate XOR for carry-free sum and shifted AND for carry, masking both to 32 bits. Convert the final sign bit to Python's signed integer interpretation.

problems.title: Reverse Integer
problems.selected_approach: Pop digits from the magnitude and push into the reversed result. Before result*10+digit, compare against a sign-specific 32-bit limit; return zero on overflow.
